key_insight: Across both spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells, photodegradation is best unified by the mobility-lifetime product (μτ), not by lifetime alone.
engineering_relevance: For scalable OSC manufacturing, preserving carrier mobility is as critical as maintaining recombination lifetime, because mobility loss can dominate efficiency decay even when lifetime increases.
method: Compared spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed PM6:Y12 devices.
Tracked performance and transport parameters during ~1000 h of continuous illumination.
Related degradation signatures to microscopic changes in morphology, recombination, and dark recovery behavior.
evidence_signal: After ~1000 h illumination, efficiency loss tracked the mobility-lifetime product μτ across both device types, with printed devices showing increased lifetime but strongly reduced mobility and added open-circuit-voltage loss from non-radiative recombination.
watch_item: The printed-architecture-specific metastable recovery indicates that degradation pathways may not transfer directly from lab-scale spin-coated devices to scalable manufacturing without architecture-specific validation.
paper_title: Mobility-lifetime relation links photodegradation in spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells
